Home / NBA News & Analysis / Portland Trail Blazers / Exclusive: Blazers’ Donovan Clingan Talks Defending Nikola Jokić Well, Damian Lillard/Dillon Brooks Dustup NBA News & Analysis Exclusive: Blazers’ Donovan Clingan Talks Defending Nikola Jokić Well, Damian Lillard/Dillon Brooks Dustup
 Portland Trail Blazers center Donovan Clingan on limiting Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokić: “I feel like I forced him to take the shots that I wanted him to take.”
 By Mark Medina Nov 10, 2026 9 min read Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images
 With a forceful pull to the ground, Portland Trail Blazers center Donovan Clingan sent two messages to Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks.
 One, don’t try to push the burly 7-foot-2, 280-pound Clingan from behind. Clingan can pull anyone down with just one of his arms easily. Two, don’t place the left leg out in front of Blazers guard Damian Lillard after taking a shot after the whistle. That will only rile up both Lillard and Clingan.
 “He cares about his teammates,” Blazers coach Micah Nori said of Clingan. “The thing with Brooks, I don’t think it was malicious. But Brooks had a little bit of a run-in with Dame, but Donovan is just protecting those guys. He quite honestly cares.”
 That care factor partly explains why the Blazers (6-3) enter Tuesday’s game against the Oklahoma City Thunder (8-2) as a viable playoff contender. Sure, Portland boasts scoring depth with Lillard, Ja Morant , Deni Avdija and Jrue Holiday . But the Blazers also feature Clingan in his third year, showing that he can hold his own against the NBA’s top centers.
 In the Blazers’ win over the Denver Nuggets last week, Clingan limited Nuggets center Nikola Jokić to a combined 5-for-13 clip as the primary defender . Clingan entered Tuesday’s games also ranking ninth in rebounds per game (10.0).
 “He’s done a really good job at a really young age with just figuring out how to play drop coverage and force tough 2s that analytically you want everyone to take,” Nori said of Clingan. “From a defensive standpoint, he’s got really good hands. He’s got really good timing. And he’s a smart player as far as playing that cat-and-mouse [game].”
 Clingan spoke to Fadeaway World about his success with defending Jokić, sticking up for Lillard after the Brooks skirmish and Morant’s spirits during his recent injury. Clingan also explained how Nori has had a positive impact as a first-year head coach and what it was like to play for Connecticut coach Dan Hurley .
 The following one-on-one conversation has been edited and condensed. 
 Why have you all gotten off to a strong start? 
 Clingan : “It’s been pretty good. The staff is putting us in a good position to succeed. We’re all executing the game plan. I feel like they’re helping us with the spacing on the floor offensively. Everyone knows their role. Everyone knows what to do on the floor. The coaches are putting us in spots so that we can execute what we’re good at. We’re doing that at a high level. Defensively, I feel like we’re trusting the coaches’ plan with what we’re trying to stop and what we’re trying to enforce. It’s all showing out there. We’re sticking together.”
 How would you assess what you’re doing individually? 
 Clingan: “I feel like it’s been a slower start. But I have picked things up. I’m starting to get a feel for the game again and understanding what my team needs from me in order to go out there and win. I’m just showing up and doing what I need to do every day.”
 What explained the slow start? 
 Clingan: “I wasn’t as active. I wasn’t moving as much. I wasn’t being the active defender, rim protector, and rebounder that I was the last few years. I really found that recently. I’ve been attacking the glass. I was being physical. I was being aggressive. I’m putting bad plays behind me.”
 You’ve been one of the league’s best rebounders. What goes into that? 
 Clingan: “I understand what I’m good at. I understand how to get good position as a rebounder and how different guys attack the glass. You start to pick up on different things, and you learn from them. I just try to be physical. I don’t take any play off. I try to go after every basketball that I can. I try to go after every ball. I then try to get good position.”
 You talked with your rookie season about the challenges with adapting to the pace of the game. How do you think you have fared since then? 
 Clingan: “I’ve definitely adapted. It’s tough as a big guy with all of our responsibilities. But I love it. I love being able to go, go, go. Being able to pick up on the pace has been good for me. We play at a very fast pace. So we’ve been picking up on that and getting in the right shape. I feel like it’s been going well.”
 When you defended Jokic this season, he was 5-for-13 from the field. What did you do reasonably well to hold him to that line? 
 Clingan: “I feel like I forced him to take the shots that I wanted him to take. I was really aggressive with him before he caught the ball. I had active hands in his face so he couldn’t see his passing options. I was also being really physical and really aggressive. I was being in his air space.”
 What was it like to take on that challenge? 
 Clingan: “I love it. I love a good challenge. I love little challenges like that. I show up, and I’m ready to play.”
 In the playoffs, you didn’t defend Wemby for a lot of minutes. But during that time, you held your own. How did you pull that off? 
 Clingan: “That was crazy. The playoffs are the playoffs. But guarding someone like that is difficult. But I’m always up for the challenge. I’m always here to compete. I tried to make him work.”
 How do you build off of your Rising Stars campaign last season? 
 Clingan: “I try to be the best defending big in the league. I try to be the best rebounder in the league. I try to be the best teammate in the league. I watch film. I stick to my game plan. I remain the player that got me here and keep doing what I’m doing to help the team win.”
 Micah said you’re great at defending in drop coverage. What’s the key to that? 
 Clingan: “Don’t let the roller get behind you. It’s important to have quick feet and make good reads. Hopefully, I can have good timing. It’s also about being active. If you’re active, you can guard.”
 Before Ja got hurt, why do you think things worked so well with him and Dame? 
 Clingan: “Everyone wants to see each other succeed. We’re all doing the right things. We’re all playing for one another. I feel like that what has gotten here.”
 How have Ja’s spirits been since his injury? 
 Clingan: “He’s been good. Obviously, it sucks that he got knocked down. But he’s staying positive. He’s been working hard. So he’ll be back better than ever.”
 You’ve raved about him as a teammate. How so? 
   Clingan: “He’s a great teammate. He’s supportive. He’s in our ears, helping us out and coaching us up. I feel like that’s what we need. He’s sharing what he sees out there and what we can do better.”
 What has Dame’s presence done for you? 
 Clingan: “With his knowledge and IQ, he shares what he sees on the floor. He’s always helping us out. He’s helping us make great big plays. It’s been crazy. He’s one of the best shooters of all time. You definitely see it.”
 What have you observed Dame doing that explains how he could come back from his Achilles injury so well? 
 Clingan: “I saw the work that he put in with everything that he did this summer and all of last year. So I knew he was going to be ready to go on day one. He has been ready.”
 What was up with the skirmish that Dillon Brooks had with you the other night? 
 Clingan: “Just standing up for my teammate [Lillard]. That’s what I do. He’s my guy.”
 Why has Deni [Avdija] adjusted so well individually, even though he’s had to change his game with Dame and Ja having some scoring and playmaking duties? 
 Clingan: “He came in and understood that there are a lot of scorers around him. But he has still stuck to his game. He has been efficient. He’s winning games for us.”
 How have you seen Jrue adjust to his bench role ? 
 Clingan : “He has great leadership. He is a two-time NBA champion. He knows what it takes to win. It’s amazing the way that Jrue carries himself. Having a championship helps. He knows and sees things before they happen. He helps us win games down the stretch. In late game, he excels on the execution part.
 Defensively and offensively, he’s able to see things. He knows the right thing to do. It really helps us. He’s won at different levels and has played the best of the best. So the things that he sees out there really, really help us.”
 Micah has had a lot of assistant-coaching stints. But why do you think he has been able to hit the ground running as a first-year head coach? 
 Clingan : “He’s a players’ coach. He understands that. He knows what we’re feeling out there. He’s playing us in great positions. He’s pushing us. He’s not taking it easy on us. If we mess up, he’s going to let us know that we’re messing up. So we’re going to step it up. He’s on our tails about doing the right thing. I feel like he really sticks to it.”
 What is he like in film sessions and practices? 
 Clingan: “He definitely is picking out things that we need to get better at. He also emphasizes stuff that we’ve done well. He’s doing a great job. I can tell that on behalf of me and all of my teammates, we all love playing for him.”
 How did Coach Hurley shape your game when you were at UConn? 
 Clingan : “ I feel like he helped me with moving my feet. He helped me with different ball-screen coverages. I also learned how to be physical. There is so much that I learned then that I know now.”
 What was it like to deal with his intensity? 
 Clingan : “Coach Hurley is Coach Hurley, man. He’s a great coach. He’s good at his job. He definitely prepared me for this level.”
